name: iron-citadel-v2
summary: ForeshadowingLoop, six rooms: the entry hall sees the guarded armory; the way round runs storeroom, forge, kitchen to the dining hall; the flank enters the armory from the hall.
The throne is reached from the hall through the library and the shrine; the vault hides off the storeroom; the cells hang off the kitchen.
A 3 x 6 grid, 3 cells empty; the best of 356 valid embeddings (1 tied).
33 enemies: 21 placed by the brief, 12 by the Director.

archetype.why: The brief's act one is a goal seen from the start and reached the long way: the entry hall sees the guarded armory (the vista on the short arc) and acts two and three reach it round the loop (way round, hall, flank). The archetype's goal is the armory; the level's goal, the throne room, lies past the hall.
archetype.short_arc: The generator makes the choke a Vista, which passes sight and no movement. The brief needs head-on to be possible ('take it head on (and die)'), so the design graph walks it: an open doorway, the guards in sight. The intent graph keeps the vista, and the Director reads that one.

rejected.why: its short arc is a sneak passage, but the brief's stealth is the long arc and its short arc is a guarded sightline; the route would also read head on
the brief has no keys; the armory is guarded, not locked
a one-way return valve; nothing in the brief is one-way
puts the goal at the antipode; the armory must sit beside the entry hall

topology.why_cycle_length: six rooms: the entry hall, a three-room thematic wing for the way round, the hall and the armory (a 2 x 3 block on the grid); eight would need a five-room wing the brief has no kinds for
topology.accept: the hall and exactly two of the three way-round rooms carry a side room: the hall's leads on to the throne, one way-round room's is the vault, the other's starts the cells
redrawn: draw 1: side rooms on [w1, w2, w3]
topology.wing_rule: side rooms on w1 and w3: the storeroom is w1 (it holds the vault), the forge w2, the kitchen w3, next to the hall
topology.intent_graph: the generator's graph plus the builder's rooms; the choke is a Vista (seen, not walked). MissionRoute and the Director read it.
topology.design_graph: the same rooms and connections with the choke Normal (walkable). The grid, the doors and the checks use it.

embedding.search: seeded backtracking (ours; PCGTools has no graph-to-grid embedder): the entry hall at the origin, rooms placed breadth-first beside a placed neighbour, every valid embedding within the bounds enumerated and scored
constraints: every room its own cell; every connection between cells sharing an edge (a wall everywhere else)
the armory east of the entry hall (a canonical turn; turning the whole level changes nothing)
the armory's two doors on facing walls, so the flank comes in behind the guards watching the entrance
the hall's way round one side anticlockwise of the armory and its way on opposite the armory: hall_gallery/back NES turned so canonical S faces the armory and canonical E takes the way round
embedding.criterion: total = 10 x far - 4 x empty + 6 x throne_at_end + 2 x enfilade + 1 x vault_walls. far: the throne room's Manhattan distance in cells from the entry hall (5 when the head-on walk to it never turns back); empty: the bounding box's empty cells (compact); throne_at_end: 1 when no room lies farther from the entry hall along the level's long axis (the throne room at the far end); enfilade: 1 when the hall, the rooms on the way to the throne and the throne room lie in one line, so the throne room's one door faces down the approach; vault_walls: the vault's sides on the outside or on an empty cell (tucked away). The seed picks among equal totals.

gaps: Rooms have no kinds, themes, states or heights in PCGTools: the fifteen kinds and their table are ours (Kinds.cs).
No wings: nothing groups rooms that belong together; the wings and the wing rule are ours.

No graph-to-grid embedder: RandomSpatialLayout places each room near its breadth-first parent without backtracking, may go diagonal and never closes a loop; the backtracking embedder and its score are ours (EmbeddingStage).
No door kinds: GateData's roles (Normal, Branch, LockedDoor, OneWayValve, SneakPassage, Vista) have no open, shut or hidden door and no secret door; the door rules are ours (DoorStage).

No 'deadly but passable' gate: ForeshadowingLoop's short arc is a Vista, which passes no movement, but the brief needs head-on to be possible; the design graph walks it and the Director reads the intent graph.

CyclicTopologyGenerator's side rooms are independent coin flips (SideRoomChance) with no way to ask for one on given rooms, so the design redraws until the hall and two way-round rooms carry one (generate and test).

DungeonGraphBuilder cannot start from an existing graph (the generator's graph is replayed connection by connection), keeps connections in a HashSet (identical connections collapse; their order is insertion order only by implementation), and Build() validates nothing.
AbstractRoom<R>._nextId is a process-wide static counter, so room ids depend on what ran earlier in the process; the design resets it to 0 before every graph.
MissionRouteResult has an internal constructor: a route cannot be written by hand, so the Director's route is the one MissionRoute measures on the intent graph.

The Director gives counts per archetype and nothing else: no post, facing or watch, and no ranged or melee meaning; with one region per room it ignores affinities, and its strongest-first fill turns small budgets ranged and large ones melee. Posts, watches and the brief's five rooms are ours.
LargestLoop finds the big loop but cannot say there is no other way round; AlternateRoutes with the armory and the way round blocked does.
No export: no JSON or SVG writer for a dungeon graph; level.json, design.json and graph.svg are ours.

armory_guards_hold_entrance.how: GateDecomposition (maxWidth 4, maxOrder 2, straightened cuts) over the walk view of armory, dining_hall, entry_hall, forge, kitchen, storeroom at one cell per 1 m column, from every entry_hall cell to every dining_hall cell; the gate nearest the d_entry_hall__armory crossing is held. HeldGrounds.AtGate reads the ground behind it (FlankScale doorway 3, passage 10, no reach cap). A guard holds the entrance when its cell is in that ground and its isovist (LaneVisibility, rho 45 cells) holds a doorway sample; a player in entry_hall sees one only at the doorway: some cell sees one, and none more than 5 m from the crossing. The player start (10-20 m back) must see the doorway and no guard; that is reported here and judged under rules.

flank_comes_in_behind.how: HeldGrounds.AtGateFrom holds the same gate from the choke guards' cells (the attackers go to the guards); FlankingRouteDetector reads its way round, which keeps off the guarded doorway, and asks that it come into their ground unseen before its last 3 cells (seen = a guard's LaneVisibility isovist, shut doors closed). Behind = the landing lies 90 degrees or more off every guard's facing (they face the doorway).

numbers.less_bar: climb route mean <= 0.5 x floor route mean

hall_floor_exposed_climb_not.how: Sight on the deck view of dining_hall at 1 m (the deck stands for its columns). The hall floor is the floor-level part of the room proper (roomy cells, not the corridors in its tile). The exposure of a cell is the share of the 4 gallery enemies whose LaneVisibility isovist (rho 45) holds it; MeanExposure, MedianExposure and MaxExposure read it along the floor route (on the walk view: the shortest walk over the hall floor between the floor cells first reached from the way-round door d_kitchen__dining_hall and from the exit d_dining_hall__library) and along the climb (on the deck view: the shortest walk from the way-round door up to the deck that keeps off the hall floor). On the walk view a column beneath the deck reads 0. ExposureField (every watcher, share of sight capacity) is reported over the floor.

numbers.as_built_reading: 0 without a second trace: nothing sees the vault even with its door open

vault_out_of_sight.how: Walk view of storeroom, treasure_vault at 1 m. The main route is the shortest walks, room by room, along the level's head_on, way_round, flank and to_throne routes inside that region. Pass: no main-route cell sees a vault cell in the LaneVisibility isovist (rho 45) with the hidden door as built (a door that is not open is a wall to sight). Reported beside it, not part of the pass: the count with the door open, and HiddenAreaDetector's reading of the vault as a pocket off its door, with the main route as trunk (door salience from the trunk's isovists) and as load (1 on the route, 0 off it).

notes: method: with every door open, each shared tile edge was scanned every 0.25 m: a crossing is NavMesh within 0.35 m of points 0.75 m either side of the edge with a clear NavMesh.Raycast between them; an edge is walkable when the run of crossings nearest its middle has a complete NavMesh path between points 1.5 m either side of it no longer than 4.5 m
